extracted.intended_audience: Contracting officers, acquisition/procurement personnel (especially DOD/Navy) and policy implementers responsible for executing OMB Circular A-76
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for applying OMB Circular A-76: assessing Commercial/Industrial Type Activities (CITAs), conducting cost comparisons, deciding in-house vs. contract performance, and implementing DOD/Navy procedures. Targets contracting officers and acquisition planners involved in CITA reviews and conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary objective of Circular A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize the primary objective to be the effective and efficient accomplishment of Government programs rather than any benefit to a particular segment of the economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circular A-76 reduced emphasis in favor of Government procurement from the private sector and clarified that program effectiveness and efficiency drive decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Government function (inherently governmental)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Government function' is one which must be performed in-house due to a special relationship in executing governmental responsibilities; examples include discretionary application of Government authority, monitoring transactions and entitlements, and maintenance of in-house core capabilities in research and development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such functions should be performed in-house regardless of private sector availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on personal services contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition of personal services contracts which create an employer-employee relationship between the Government and the contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circular prohibits conversions or contract actions that would result in an improper employer-employee relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circular summary exception rule (three new exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The new circular clarifies and combines prior five exceptions into three: (1) No satisfactory commercial source is available to perform the service which includes any delay and disruption to ongoing Government programs; (2) It is in the interest of National Defense to maintain the capacity within the Government; (3) The Government can perform the service or provide the product at a lower cost than the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three exceptions define when in-house performance may be justified; prior five exceptions are consolidated into these.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation required for nonavailability of commercial sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification due to nonavailability of commercial sources requires extensive documentation of attempts to locate or develop an adequate commercial source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a minimum, announcements must be made in the Commerce Business Daily and assistance should be sought from GSA, SBA, and similar organizations. Possibility of strikes, urgency, or classification alone are not sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Defense justification standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification for a Government CITA on the basis of National Defense must be to satisfy training requirements or career development and rotation patterns of military personnel; personnel—civilian or military—must be utilized in a direct combat support role or needed to maintain a core capability in intermediate or depot level maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such justifications must be approved at the Military Department Assistant Secretary level (e.g., Navy: ASN (MRA&L)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rules for cost comparison (use same SOW and level of performance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of the same scope of work and level of performance in analysis of in-house and contract out costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOW used for contractor solicitations must form the basis for the Government in-house cost estimate to ensure comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rules (standard cost factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of the standard cost factors as specified in the Cost Comparison Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must apply the handbook's specified factors to achieve uniformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rules (full costing for Government estimate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of full costing in preparation of the Government estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government in-house cost estimates must be fully burdened per handbook guidance to be comparable with contract prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rules (pre-priced options to preclude buy-ins)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to use pre-priced options to the maximum extent possible to preclude 'buy-ins' and allow amortization of contractor start up costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-priced options help prevent artificially low initial bids that are recovered through options and permit fair treatment of contractor startup cost amortization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rules (firm bids with intent to award)
rubrics_metrics.description: The contract price must be obtained by soliciting firm bids or proposals from the private sector with the full intent to award a contract if it is more cost effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicitations must be realistic and conducted as genuine competitions to determine true contract prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dollar threshold for cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Raises the dollar limit from $50,000 to $100,000 for which a cost comparison is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No in-house activity valued in excess of $100,000 will be converted to contract performance unless justified by a cost study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion differentials (existing in-house vs new starts)
rubrics_metrics.description: An existing in-house activity will not be converted to contract performance unless such conversion will result in savings of more than 10% of estimated Government personnel costs. Conversely, a new start will be contracted-out unless the potential savings by Government in-house performance are greater than 10% of Government personnel costs plus 25% of equipment and facilities costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differential is designed to maintain status quo for existing in-house work but favors contracting-out for all new programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of other agency services and set-asides
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular provides for the use of services from another agency if there is a formal program established to utilize excess capacity. The Circular specifically encourages set-aside programs for small businesses (including those owned/managed by disadvantaged persons). Contracts previously awarded under set-aside programs will not be reviewed again for possible in-house performance; new requirements suitable for a set-aside should be offered for contract without cost comparison analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for interagency excess capacity and protection of set-aside awards from re-review; new suitable set-asides bypass cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory compilation and review schedule requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to compile a complete inventory of all CITAs to be updated annually with greater reporting detail. Agencies must establish an initial three year review schedule, publish it for review by the general public, and for activities approved for retention in-house schedule follow-on reviews at least once every five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More definitive review schedules replace prior triennial requirement; inventories and schedules must be publicized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative procedures for dispute/review of in-house/contract decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative procedures must be established in each agency to resolve questions on in-house/contract decisions. Upon written request from an affected party, the agency must have the decision reviewed by an official of the same or higher level than the official who approved the initial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewing official must assure decisions are fair and equitable and comply with Circular guidelines; the decisions of the reviewing official are final and not subject to arbitration, negotiation or other agreements; applies only to the decision to contract-out vs perform in-house (not to contract award disputes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using personnel ceilings to justify conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular will not be used to justify conversion solely on the basis of personnel ceiling restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversions must be based on the Circular's substantive criteria, not to circumvent personnel ceilings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using Circular inconsistently with laws/treaties/agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular will not be used when it is inconsistent with any laws, treaties, or international agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal/international obligations supersede Circular-driven conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to use the Cost Comparison Handbook (Supplement No.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes 'common ground rules' for analyzing both Government in-house and contractor costs including the use of Supplement No.1 to the Circular, the 'Cost Comparison Handbook,' in all instances where a cost comparison is to be prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handbook provides detailed guidance necessary to compare in-house and contract costs on an equitable basis; agencies must follow it to ensure uniformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: CITA definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A commercial or industrial type activity is one which is managed and operated by a Federal agency and produces goods or services which could be obtained from a private source including commercial concerns, universities and other non-federal activities located in the United States, its territories and possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines scope of activities subject to A-76 review and inventorying.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD implementation duties (public schedules & congressional notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSD directed the services to: (1) prepare three year review schedules for public release; (2) identify FY functions to be studied for public release; (3) make Congressional notice of inventory schedules as required by the DOD Authorizations Act; and (4) make Congressional notification prior to award of contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation requires transparency to public and Congress as part of CITA management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navy fact sheet and CNO approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: Navy uses fact sheets from each activity to identify functions for review; receipt of the fact sheet at CNO indicates no compelling reason to retain in-house. CNO approval and return provides authority to proceed with solicitation. Additionally, an assessment of EEO impact must be provided and no contracts or RIF notices will be issued until specific CNO approval message is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized Navy control: CNO/CNM roles, requirement for EEO impact assessment, and hold on awards/RIFs until approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm bid/offer procedure in support of CITA program
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of firm bid/offer procedure (as promulgated in NAVMAT PPM No.49 and NAVSUPINST 4280.6) to obtain contract prices and guidance as to contracting officer responsibilities in that procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs contracting officers on responsibilities when using firm bid/offer in the cost comparison process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison process steps & responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparison process: establish Task Group to prepare plan/schedule and detailed SOW; SOW used for contractor solicitations and Government in-house cost estimate; contractors submit bids/proposals while Task Group prepares sealed audited in-house estimate; determine low contract price and adjust it to reflect true Government cost; complete and certify cost comparison; audit; possible pre-award survey; Task Group recommendation to Approving Authority; Approving Authority decision; public announcement and review period; award or cancel solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities: AA (Approving Authority), IA (Independent Auditor), TG (Task Group), PC (Prospective Contractor), CO (Contracting Officer). Many CO tasks fall within and beyond this process (e.g., notices in CDB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealing and auditing of in-house cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government cost estimate is audited for accuracy and conformance to prescribed guidelines, sealed, and submitted to the Contracting Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sealed Government estimate protects integrity of the comparison; independent audit ensures conformance to handbook rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusting contract price to reflect true Government cost
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the cost comparison, it will be necessary to adjust the 'contract price' to reflect the true cost to the Government for private sector performance of the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract price adjustments account for differences between contractor bid prices and the actual Government burdened cost of contract performance (startup costs, amortization, options, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award survey when private cost appears lower
rubrics_metrics.description: If the total private industry cost appears lower than the Government in-house cost estimate, the Contracting Officer may conduct a pre-award survey on the lower offerer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-award surveys verify contractor capability and proposed cost/pricing assumptions before award decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer responsibilities beyond solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers have responsibilities prior to receipt of purchase request (e.g., place notices in the Commerce Business Daily when lack of satisfactory commercial source is claimed) and should assess internal organization, staffing and workload to prepare for implementation of policy guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CO duties include planning, public notices, and actions that may prevent a purchase request from ever reaching the contracting office.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAO-identified implementation problem areas
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO cited problems impeding policy implementation: (1) lack of clear executive and legislative branch support; (2) inconsistent and ineffective implementation by departments/agencies; (3) decisions not always made on strictly economic basis; (4) influence by personnel ceilings; (5) reluctance by agencies to carry out the policy; (6) agencies' difficulty in knowing when/how to accomplish cost comparisons; (7) lack of clear understanding which programs are commercial/industrial activities; (8) required reviews far behind schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These findings identify weaknesses to be addressed for effective A-76 implementation and serve as criteria for evaluating program performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Secretarial approval for major new starts/expansions
rubrics_metrics.description: The new Circular provides more complete definitions of 'new starts' and 'expansions' of existing in-house capabilities and requires Assistant Secretarial approval for activities which will require a large initial capital investment by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-capital activities need senior-level approval before proceeding.
